quick: Apply a thin layer to affected skin once or twice daily (0.05% cream/ointment)
Use only if necessary; smallest amount for shortest time
Caution; avoid applying to breast/nipple before feeds
Skin atrophy, local effects; signs of systemic absorption with large areas
summary: Clobetasone butyrate is a moderately potent topical corticosteroid (0.05%) used for inflammatory and pruritic dermatoses such as eczema and dermatitis, and as an ophthalmic preparation for ocular inflammation. It has a relatively favourable benefit-to-risk profile among topical steroids. It is not FDA-approved; use and dosing follow EMA/SmPC and BNF guidance.
indications: Eczema and dermatitis of various causes including atopic and primary irritant/allergic dermatitis
Prurigo nodularis, lichen simplex, and other steroid-responsive inflammatory dermatoses
Ophthalmic: short-term treatment of ocular inflammation (where approved)

dosage.d: Apply a thin film once or twice daily
Apply thinly once or twice daily for short courses
dosage.n: Limit area, duration and potency in children

admin: Apply a thin layer only to affected areas and rub in gently
Wash hands after application unless the hands are being treated
Do not use under occlusive dressings unless directed
Use the smallest amount for the shortest time needed to control symptoms
Avoid the face and skin folds for prolonged periods
moa: Clobetasone butyrate is a glucocorticoid that binds intracellular corticosteroid receptors, modulating gene transcription to produce anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, antiproliferative and vasoconstrictive effects. It reduces inflammatory mediator release, leukocyte infiltration and capillary permeability in the skin.

absolute: Untreated cutaneous bacterial, viral or fungal infection
relative: Application to the face for prolonged periods
Use on large areas or under occlusion

preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; apply the smallest amount over the smallest area for the shortest time. Avoid extensive or prolonged use.
lact: Can be used with caution; avoid applying directly to the breast or nipple before breastfeeding and avoid large amounts.
renal: No dose adjustment needed for topical use.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed for topical use.

moderate: Other topical agents on the same area (altered absorption)
minor: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (theoretical increased systemic steroid effect with extensive use)
interactions.diagnostics: Extensive use may suppress HPA axis affecting cortisol/ACTH testing

common: Local burning, stinging or itching on application
serious: Skin atrophy, striae and telangiectasia with prolonged use
Glaucoma/cataract with ophthalmic or periocular use
rare: Allergic contact dermatitis to the product

monitoring: Signs of skin thinning, striae or telangiectasia
Intraocular pressure if used in or near the eye
Signs of systemic absorption if used on large areas, under occlusion or in children
counsel: Apply only a thin layer to the affected skin as directed
Do not use on infected, broken or facial skin unless told to
Do not use for longer than advised - long-term use can thin the skin
Wash hands after applying unless treating the hands
This medicine is not FDA-approved; follow your local product information
pk: Anti-inflammatory effect within hours to a few days
Local effect builds over days of regular use
Minimal systemic exposure with correct topical use
Sustained with continued application; taper as condition improves
Store below 25 C; do not freeze
pearls: Not FDA-approved; widely used in the UK/EU (e.g., Eumovate) per BNF/SmPC - include this caveat when advising
Moderately potent steroid with a comparatively favourable benefit-to-risk ratio - useful step-down from potent steroids
Avoid prolonged facial use and large-area/occlusive use to limit atrophy and systemic absorption
Ophthalmic clobetasone (e.g., Cloburate) requires intraocular pressure monitoring
missed: For a missed application, apply it when remembered, then continue as before. Do not apply extra to make up a missed dose.
overdose: Topical overdose or chronic overuse can cause local skin atrophy and, rarely, systemic corticosteroid effects (HPA-axis suppression, Cushingoid features). Discontinue gradually if extensive systemic effects occur; treat skin changes supportively.
